subject: ss-cardiology
title: Supraventricular tachycardias and preexcitation: mechanism, pharmacotherapy and ablation

steps.tx: **AV nodal reentrant tachycardia** represents the most common regular supraventricular tachycardia, sustained by dual AV nodal physiology. Typical slow-fast AVNRT involves antegrade conduction down the slow pathway and retrograde conduction up the fast pathway, producing simultaneous atrial and ventricular activation with pseudo-r prime in V1 and pseudo-S in inferior leads.
steps.say: Atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia is the most frequent regular supraventricular tachycardia, sustained by functional dual atrioventricular nodal pathways. Typical slow-fast AVNRT utilizes the slow pathway for antegrade conduction and the fast pathway for retrograde conduction, showing pseudo r prime in lead V1.

steps.tx: Intravenous **adenosine** is the first-line pharmacologic therapy for terminating acute regular narrow-complex supraventricular tachycardias. Given as a rapid 6 mg IV bolus followed by 12 mg if required, adenosine activates A1 adenosine receptors, opening inward potassium channels and producing transient complete AV nodal conduction block to interrupt the reentrant circuit.
steps.say: Intravenous adenosine is the first line pharmacologic agent for terminating acute regular narrow complex supraventricular tachycardia. Administered as a rapid six milligram intravenous bolus followed by twelve milligrams if needed, adenosine stimulates A1 receptors to cause transient atrioventricular nodal block.

rows: 6 mg rapid IV push + 20 mL saline flush
12 mg rapid IV push if no termination in 2 min
Terminates remaining responsive nodal reentrant SVTs

steps.tx: Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome features ventricular **preexcitation** on baseline ECG, characterized by a short PR interval < 120 ms, slurred QRS upstroke (delta wave), and widened QRS duration > 120 ms, reflecting antegrade conduction over an accessory pathway bypassing the physiologic delay of the AV node.
steps.say: Wolff Parkinson White syndrome displays ventricular preexcitation on the resting electrocardiogram, characterized by a short PR interval under 120 milliseconds, a slurred initial QRS upstroke known as a delta wave, and widened QRS duration reflecting antegrade conduction across an anomalous accessory pathway.

rows: Opposite in direction to delta wave

steps.tx: The resting tracing shows the **ventricular preexcitation** triad of **short PR interval** and **delta wave** with a broad fused QRS. The inset labels a PR below 120 ms, a slurred takeoff into the tall complex, and total width above 120 ms. Spotting this triad matters because it reveals an accessory pathway that bypasses normal nodal delay and sets the stage for rapid reentrant rhythms.
steps.say: This tracing shows the classic WPW pattern at rest. The PR gap is short, the start of the QRS looks slurred upward like a small hump, and the whole QRS looks wide. That slurred hump is the delta wave. Recognizing it matters because it tells you an extra electrical connection exists that can carry very fast rhythms.

vis.alt: A 12 lead ECG labeled Wolff Parkinson White pattern shows normal rhythm with an inset magnifying a short PR interval, a slurred delta wave takeoff, and a wide QRS complex.
vis.caption: Resting ECG showing short PR interval with delta wave and wide QRS Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Orthodromic AVRT** conducts antegrade down the normal AV node and His-Purkinje system and retrograde up the accessory pathway, producing a narrow-complex tachycardia. Conversely, antidromic AVRT conducts antegrade down the accessory pathway and retrograde up the AV node, producing a wide-complex fully preexcited tachycardia mimicking ventricular tachycardia.
steps.say: Orthodromic atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia conducts antegrade down the normal AV node and retrograde up the accessory pathway, generating a narrow complex tachycardia. Antidromic AVRT conducts antegrade down the accessory pathway and retrograde up the AV node, producing a wide complex tachycardia mimicking ventricular tachycardia.

left.title: Orthodromic AVRT
points: Antegrade AV node, retrograde accessory pathway; narrow QRS complex (< 120 ms), accounts for 90% of AVRT.

right.title: Antidromic AVRT
points: Antegrade accessory pathway, retrograde AV node; wide regular QRS complex (>= 120 ms), accounts for < 10% of AVRT.

steps.tx: **procainamide**: Preexcited atrial fibrillation in WPW presents with an irregular, wide-complex tachycardia with bizarre variable QRS morphology and ventricular rates exceeding 250 to 300 bpm. Rapid antegrade conduction down the accessory pathway can trigger ventricular fibrillation and sudden cardiac death.
steps.say: Preexcited atrial fibrillation in Wolff Parkinson White syndrome manifests as an irregularly irregular, wide complex tachycardia with polymorphic QRS complexes and ventricular rates exceeding 250 to 300 beats per minute. Rapid accessory pathway conduction can degenerate into fatal ventricular fibrillation.

steps.tx: In preexcited atrial fibrillation, **AV nodal blocking agents are strictly contraindicated**, including adenosine, beta-blockers, non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers, and digitalis. Blocking the AV node preferentially shunts fibrillatory impulses down the rapidly conducting accessory pathway, precipitating ventricular fibrillation and cardiac arrest.
steps.say: In preexcited atrial fibrillation, atrioventricular nodal blocking drugs, including adenosine, beta blockers, verapamil, and digoxin, are strictly contraindicated. Blocking AV nodal conduction accelerates conduction down the accessory pathway, directly precipitating ventricular fibrillation. Detailed mastery of these diagnostic thresholds and hemodynamic criteria is essential for clinical examination excellence.

left.title: Contraindicated Drugs
points: Adenosine, verapamil, diltiazem, beta-blockers, digoxin; accelerate pathway conduction toward ventricular fibrillation.

right.title: Indicated Management
points: Direct current electrical cardioversion if hemodynamically unstable; intravenous procainamide or ibutilide if stable.

steps.tx: **Antidromic AVRT**: Definitive curative therapy for recurrent AVNRT or WPW with accessory pathways is catheter ablation. Slow pathway modification in the inferior triangle of Koch cures AVNRT with > 95% success and < 1% risk of complete AV block, while accessory pathway ablation eliminates preexcitation and abolishes sudden death risk.
steps.say: Definitive curative therapy for recurrent atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia and accessory pathways is radiofrequency catheter ablation. Slow pathway modification in the triangle of Koch cures AVNRT with over 95 percent success, while accessory pathway ablation permanently abolishes sudden death risk.

rows: Inferior triangle of Koch (coronary sinus os to tricuspid annulus)
Mitral annulus (transseptal or retrograde aortic approach)

steps.tx: **High-risk accessory pathways** in asymptomatic WPW are identified during electrophysiology study by an accessory pathway effective refractory period <= 250 ms or shortest preexcited RR interval in AF <= 250 ms. These markers identify high risk of sudden cardiac death and constitute a Class I indication for catheter ablation.
steps.say: High risk accessory pathways in Wolff Parkinson White syndrome are identified during electrophysiologic testing by an accessory pathway effective refractory period of 250 milliseconds or less, or a shortest preexcited RR interval in atrial fibrillation of 250 milliseconds or less, mandating catheter ablation.

rows: Class I indication for catheter ablation
High risk of rapid conduction into VF
